prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Reordering sign_in steps was helpful in 3 winning tests (+9.0%, +4.3%, and +4.8% after noise correction), while 5 other tests showed no clear effect.
Adding a new screen to adoption was harmful, as both tests agreed on a negative impact after noise correction (-2.5% and -10.4%).
Evidence is still thin for adoption redesign and finish new_screen changes because their tests disagreed after noise correction.
Evidence is still thin for adoption hint, home new_flow, and choose_path reorder changes because each has only 1 test.
Predictions were generally too high across most tests, particularly for tests with no clear effect or those stopped early.
Predictions were too low for the round 2 finish new_screen test (+8.0% predicted vs +9.8% noise-corrected) and round 8 sign_in reorder test (+0.8% predicted vs +9.0% noise-corrected).

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, hint: -5.9% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- adoption, new_screen: -5.8% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- adoption, redesign: -4.1% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- choose_path, reorder: -2.8% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: +0.3% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- home, new_flow: -10.9% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: +2.0% after noise correction, 8 test(s)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 87.7%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 77.0%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 25.5%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [sign_in, reorder] Sign-In Relocation Post Waiting Stage: Moves the sign-in step to occur after pet generation waiting stage right before home introduction. (why: Reordering sign-in later improved completion across 3 prior winning tests. Letting users generate their pet first increases commitment before requiring account login.)
1: [choose_path, redesign] Spotlight Layout Choose Path Stage: Redesigns the choose_path screen into a spotlight view focusing on pre-made vs custom pet path choices. (why: Choose path has a median time of 8s but mean of 514s, indicating confusion or idle drop-off. A spotlight layout highlights the immediate choice clearly.)
2: [sign_in, hint] Sign-In Account Synchronization Hint: Adds an informational hint on the sign-in screen explaining that signing in syncs pet data to prevent reset. (why: Support receives 8 emails regarding pets missing or reset after signing back in. Clarifying sync state upfront prevents account confusion.)
3: [finish, new_screen] Pre-Home Companion Ready Summary Screen: Inserts a new confirmation screen right before home intro summarizing the companion setup. (why: Adding finish screens has shown strong positive impact (+9.8% noise-corrected) in earlier tests, helping bridge onboarding into desktop display.)
4: [home, wait_info] Waiting Stage Progress and Time Info: Displays progress indicator and estimated wait time during pet rendering on the waiting screen. (why: The adoption and waiting stages take high mean time (1017s) and suffer drop-off. Providing progress feedback keeps users engaged while waiting.)
5: [adoption, layout] Adoption Certificate Centered Layout Refinement: Changes adoption certificate layout to centered mode with an official verification badge. (why: Adoption stage has the lowest step conversion (60.9%). A centered certificate design reinforces the emotional reward of adopting a pet.)
6: [choose_path, new_flow] Mascot Desktop Journey Introduction Flow: Adds a mascot welcome screen at the start of onboarding to set expectations before path selection. (why: Overall onboarding conversion is 25.5%. Introducing a friendly mascot intro screen at the start sets clear visual context and improves early completion.)
7: [adoption, copy] Upload Photos Clarity Copy Update: Updates photo upload screen instructions and hint with clear guidance on photo quality. (why: 3 support tickets reported custom pet generation failures or visual glitches. Clear photo guidelines prevent generation issues.)
8: [home, notification] Waiting Stage Completion Notification Switch: Enables desktop ready notifications and a auto-tip on the waiting screen when processing finishes. (why: Users wait a median of 201s during home setup. Notification alerts ensure users return if they switch to other desktop windows.)

scores.note: Reordering sign-in post pet creation has strong historical support with 3 winning tests (+2.0% average lift).
Choose path has huge mean vs median time gap (514s vs 8s), but redesign evidence remains unproven.
Supported directly by 8 user emails regarding account sync confusion; low implementation cost.
Requires a new screen (cost 0). Previous finish new_screen test showed +9.8% but evidence overall is thin.
Home step has a long 201s median / 2336s mean wait time; progress info reduces drop-off during generation.
Adoption has highest drop-off (60.9% pass), but prior adoption redesigns consistently dropped conversion (-4.1%).
Adding new introductory flows/screens previously harmed conversion (home new_flow was -10.9%).
Adoption loses 39.1% of users and 3 support tickets highlight generation failures from bad photo uploads.
High mean wait time (2336s) on home step indicates tab-switching; notifications help bring users back.
